system: You are a helpful assistant. Notes and summaries can drift from what they summarise. Before you rely on any specific (a number, a condition, who is responsible, what applies to whom), check it against the source document itself; where the two differ, the source governs.
message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Halden's Records Retention and Deletion Policy (IG-03 v2.1, March 2026) sets how long personal data and business records are kept under UK GDPR. The DPO owns the policy, keeps the schedule and approves exceptions. The IT Service Desk is responsible for deleting records once their retention period ends, with line managers making sure staff comply. Key periods: unsuccessful job applicants, 12 months after the decision (talent-pool members 12 months from consent); personnel files, 6 years after leaving; payroll and tax, 6 years after the tax year; accident book, 3 years (longer for minors); CCTV, 30 days unless linked to an incident reported to police or Legal; customer service call recordings, 90 days; complaint files, 3 years after closure; marketing consents, while active plus 2 years; loyalty data, 26 months then anonymised. Legal holds override the schedule until lifted. Paper goes to cross-cut shredding; electronic records are deleted from live systems and purged from backups within 90 days. Subject access requests go to the DPO the same day and are answered within one month (extendable by two for complex cases). Suspected breaches go to the DPO immediately, who reports to the ICO within 72 hours if required. Departments confirm their annual review by 31 January.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
HALDEN RETAIL GROUP — RECORDS RETENTION AND DELETION POLICY (Policy IG-03, Version 2.1, approved by the Board, 12 March 2026)

1. Purpose. This policy sets the periods for which Halden keeps personal data and business records, in line with UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018. Data must not be kept for longer than necessary for the purpose for which it was collected.

2. Responsibilities. The Data Protection Officer (DPO) owns this policy, maintains the retention schedule and approves any exceptions. Each department has an Information Asset Owner (IAO), normally the head of department, who is responsible for ensuring that records held by that department are reviewed and deleted at the end of their retention period. The IT Service Desk carries out technical deletion from central systems only when instructed by an IAO; IT does not decide what is deleted and does not delete departmental records automatically. Line managers are responsible for ensuring staff follow this policy.

3. Retention schedule (extract). • Recruitment — unsuccessful applicants: 6 months after the date the applicant was told of the decision, then deleted. Applicants who give explicit consent to join our talent pool are kept for 12 months from consent. • Employee personnel files: 6 years after employment ends. • Payroll and tax records: 6 years after the end of the tax year to which they relate. • Accident book entries: 3 years after the entry, or until the injured person reaches 21 if they were a minor. • CCTV footage (stores and warehouses): 30 days, then automatically overwritten, unless footage relates to an incident that has been reported to the police or to the Legal team, in which case it is retained until the matter is closed. • Customer service call recordings: 90 days. Recordings of calls to the Halden Money (consumer credit) desk are kept for 5 years because of Financial Conduct Authority requirements. • Customer complaint files: 3 years after the complaint is closed. • Marketing consent records: for as long as the consent is active, plus 2 years after withdrawal. • Loyalty card transaction data: 26 months after the last transaction, then anonymised.

4. Legal holds. Where litigation or a regulatory investigation is reasonably anticipated, the Legal team may place a hold on relevant records. Records subject to a hold must not be deleted, even if their retention period has expired, until Legal lifts the hold.

5. Method of deletion. Paper records must be placed in confidential waste consoles for cross-cut shredding. Electronic records must be deleted from live systems and will be purged from backups within 90 days through the normal backup cycle.

6. Subject access requests. Requests from individuals for copies of their data must be passed to the DPO on the day of receipt. Halden will respond within one calendar month, extendable by two further months for complex requests.

7. Breaches. Suspected data breaches must be reported to the DPO immediately. The DPO will decide whether the breach must be reported to the Information Commissioner's Office, and will do so within 72 hours of Halden becoming aware of it where required.

8. Annual review. Each IAO must confirm to the DPO by 31 January each year that the department's records have been reviewed against this schedule.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. Within how long must Halden respond to a subject access request?
2. Our Marketing department has old customer spreadsheets past their retention date. Whose job is it to make sure they get deleted?
3. A candidate we rejected nine months ago, who did not join the talent pool, asks if we still hold her CV. Should we?
4. A customer complains about what she was told on a call to the Halden Money credit desk eight months ago. Should a recording still exist?
response:
Checked against the policy itself. My earlier notes had three errors, flagged below.

**1. Subject access requests:** Halden must respond within **one calendar month**, extendable by **two further months** for complex requests (s.6). The request must also go to the DPO on the day it's received.

**2. Marketing's old spreadsheets:** It's the job of **Marketing's Information Asset Owner (IAO)**, normally the head of Marketing. The IAO must make sure the department's records are reviewed and deleted at the end of their retention period (s.2).
- The IT Service Desk only deletes from central systems **when instructed by an IAO**. It doesn't decide what is deleted and doesn't delete departmental records automatically.
- Line managers make sure staff follow the policy, but the deletion responsibility sits with the IAO.
- *My notes were wrong here.* They said IT was responsible for deletion.

**3. Rejected candidate, nine months ago, not in the talent pool:** **No, her CV should not still be held.** Unsuccessful applicants are kept for **6 months** after they were told of the decision, then deleted (s.3). At nine months it is overdue for deletion.
- *My notes were wrong here.* They said 12 months, which would have suggested keeping it. The 12-month period applies only to talent-pool members, from the date of consent.
- Before deleting, check that no **legal hold** applies (s.4), for example a discrimination claim. If she has asked whether you hold her CV, treat this as a possible subject access request and pass it to the DPO today. Don't delete the CV while that request is being handled.

**4. Halden Money call from eight months ago:** **Yes, a recording should still exist.** Ordinary customer service recordings are kept for 90 days, but calls to the **Halden Money (consumer credit) desk are kept for 5 years** because of FCA requirements (s.3).
- *My notes left this exception out.* Relying on them would have suggested the recording was deleted long ago.
- Since this is now a complaint, the complaint file will be kept for 3 years after closure. If Legal thinks a dispute is likely, ask them about a legal hold.
